extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners involved in preparing or processing Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs)
extracted.subtask_short: filing an IDS with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and best-practices for preparing and timely filing an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) under 37 CFR 1.97–1.98, including content, format, copies, translations, electronic submission rules, and timing windows during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: General statutory/content compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement (IDS) must comply with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.98 as to content for the information listed in the IDS to be considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide attempt is made to comply with 37 CFR 1.98 but part of the required content is inadvertently omitted, additional time may be given to enable full compliance pursuant to 37 CFR 1.97(f). See MPEP § 609.04(b), subsection VI and form paragraph 6.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS must include a separate list of all cited items
rubrics_metrics.description: Each IDS must include a list of all patents, publications, U.S. applications, or other information submitted for consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list must be submitted on a separate paper (not incorporated into the specification) so the Office can confirm applicant intends to submit an IDS and so examiners have a readily available checklist. Use of form PTO/SB/08 is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS listing format per 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDS listing must follow a specified format: (A) specified format/identification for each page and U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications listed in a section separately from other documents; (B) a column providing space next to each document for the examiner’s initials; and (C) a heading that identifies the list as an IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications from other citations permits OCR of U.S. patent numbers and publication numbers for electronic availability. Each page should be clearly labeled as an IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each page must identify the application number
rubrics_metrics.description: Each page of the list must clearly identify the application number of the application in which the IDS is being submitted, if known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include the correct application number on each page (e.g., use of forms from other applications) can prevent association of pages with the proper application if pages become separated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Column for examiner initials
rubrics_metrics.description: The list must include a column that provides a space next to each document listed to permit the examiner to enter their initials next to the citations of the documents that have been considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a clear record indicating which documents have been considered. Applicants are discouraged from submitting completed PTO/SB/08 forms from other applications which may already bear other examiners’ initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for U.S. patents
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patents must be identified by the inventor, patent number, and issue date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the information in a way that permits accurate identification by the Office and OCR systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for U.S. patent application publications
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patent application publications must be identified by the applicant, patent application publication number, and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will also accept identification using the inventor instead of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for U.S. applications
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. applications must be identified by the inventor, the eight digit application number (two digit series code and six digit serial number), and the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a U.S. application listed in an IDS has been issued as a patent or published, the applicant should list the patent or application publication in the IDS instead of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for foreign patents and published foreign applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each foreign patent or published foreign patent application must be identified by the country or patent office which issued/published it, an appropriate document number, and the publication date indicated on the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the same identifying detail as shown on the foreign document to permit accurate retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for publications/non‑patent literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication must be identified by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages of the publication, and date and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no page numbers are supplied, it is understood that all pages are relevant. The date of publication should include at least the month and year; a year alone is acceptable only if the applicant points out that the month is not material relative to effective U.S. filing or priority dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite pending U.S. applications and other office documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending U.S. applications cited can be listed under non-patent literature or in a separate appropriately labeled section; Office actions or other materials from an application should be listed separately under non-patent literature or a new section appropriately labeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO is understood to be the publisher/place of publication for U.S. Office actions or U.S. applications; foreign entities (WIPO, EPO) are understood to be the publisher/place for their search reports or actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet publications: URL and retrieval information
rubrics_metrics.description: For publications obtained from the internet, the URL of the webpage that is the source must be provided as the place of publication; when actual publication date not known, provide at minimum a date of retrieval or a time frame when the document was available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the document is from an archived webpage, provide both the URL of the archived webpage submitted and the URL of the site from which the archived copy was obtained (provide retrieval dates). See MPEP § 707.05(e) for examples including social media and video screenshots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate list requirement (not incorporated in specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of information complying with 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) and 1.98(b) may not be incorporated into the specification and must be submitted in a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate list makes intent clear and provides an examiner checklist. Use form PTO/SB/08 when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legible copy requirements (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each IDS must include legible copies of: (A) each foreign patent; (B) each publication or the portion which caused it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required); (C) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including claims and any drawings, or the portion that caused it to be listed, unless the cited pending U.S. application is stored in IFW; and (D) all other information or the portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no general requirement for copies of U.S. patents or U.S. patent application publications unless the Office requires them. If material other than spec/claims/drawings in a cited pending U.S. application is being cited (e.g., Office action), copies of such material must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW waiver for pending U.S. application copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for a legible copy of the specification, including claims, and drawings of each cited pending U.S. patent application is sua sponte waived where the cited pending application is stored in the USPTO’s Image File Wrapper (IFW) system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The waiver is limited to the specification, claims, and drawings. If other material in the file is being cited, copies of that material are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception when prior application already submitted the information (37 CFR 1.98(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any patent, publication, pending U.S. application, or other information listed in an IDS is not required to be provided if: (A) the information was previously cited by or submitted to the Office in a prior application, provided the prior application is properly identified in the IDS and is relied on for an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120; and (B) the prior IDS complied with 37 CFR 1.98(a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception does not apply to information cited in an international application under the PCT. If the prior-submitted information was not in English, a concise explanation of relevance need not be provided unless its relevance differs from that in the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative references rule (37 CFR 1.98(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosures of two or more patents or publications listed in an IDS are substantively cumulative, a copy of one of the patents/publications may be submitted without copies of the others provided a statement is made that the others are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will consider only the patent/publication of which a copy is submitted and will so indicate on the list (e.g., by crossing out cumulative listings). Beware that a withheld reference may not be cumulative if it discloses a more complete relevant combination (Semiconductor Energy Laboratory Co. v. Samsung Electronics Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and English copy rule for non-English documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a written English translation of a non-English document (or portion) is in the possession, custody, or control of, or is readily available to, any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c), a copy of the translation shall accompany the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations are not required to be verified; translations must be actual translations of what is contained in the non-English information. If no translation is submitted, the examiner will consider the information in view of any concise explanation and insofar as it is understood on its face (e.g., drawings, formulas, English abstracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise explanation of relevance for non‑English information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each IDS must include a concise explanation of the relevance, as presently understood by the individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) most knowledgeable about the content of the non-English information listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concise explanation may be separate from the specification or part of it (if so, the IDS listing should include page/line numbers). If a complete translation is submitted, no concise explanation is required. An English-language abstract or a foreign search report/action indicating relevance (e.g., X/Y/A indications) may satisfy the requirement. Do not submit partial translations or concise explanations that are intended to misdirect the examiner (Semiconductor Energy). Applicants are encouraged to provide concise explanations for English-language information as well when helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission limitations and permitted electronic materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic means for filing IDSs are not permitted except for: (A) IDSs electronically submitted using the USPTO patent electronic filing system (EFS); or (B) copies of large tables, computer program listings, and sequence listings submitted as a PDF file and a 'Sequence Listing XML' submitted as XML on a read-only optical disc in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e)(2) and (3) which are cited in a paper IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A read-only optical disc cannot be used to submit an IDS listing or ordinary copies of documents cited in the IDS (except the specified large files). Visual output or video must be reduced to writing (screenshots, transcripts) to be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early filing window: within three months or before first Office action (37 CFR 1.97(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS will be considered by the examiner if filed within one of the specified early time periods: (A) for national applications, within three months of filing or before mailing of the first Office action on the merits; (B) for international applications, within three months of national stage entry or before first Office action on the merits; (C) for RCEs and CPAs, before the mailing date of a first Office action on the merits; (D) for international design applications, within three months of publication under Hague Article 10(3) or before first Office action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS filed within these periods requires neither a fee nor a statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e) and will be considered. The filing date is the date received in the Office (or earlier mailing date if accompanied by a proper certificate of mailing/facsimile or Priority Mail Express compliance). If the last day falls on weekend/holiday, timely filing may be the next business day per 37 CFR 1.7(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after early window but before prosecution closes (37 CFR 1.97(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed after the early period but before prosecution closes (before mailing of a final Office action, Notice of Allowance, or Ex parte Quayle action) will be considered if accompanied by either (1) a statement as specified in 37 CFR 1.97(e) or (2) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information submitted during this period with a 1.97(e) statement is used in a new ground of rejection on unamended claims, the next Office action will not be made final (applicant submitted the information promptly). If the new ground was necessitated by amendment of the application, final rejection may be appropriate. If submitted with the fee, the examiner may use the information and make the next Office action final (subject to MPEP § 706.07(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after final/allowance but before payment of issue fee (37 CFR 1.97(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed on or after mailing of a final action, Notice of Allowance, or action that closes prosecution but before or simultaneous with payment of the issue fee will be considered provided it is accompanied by (A) a statement as specified in 37 CFR 1.97(e) and (B) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements reflect the late stage of prosecution. Such an IDS will be handled as a 'Printer Rush' (see MPEP § 1309.02). Form paragraph 6.52 may be used to inform applicant that the IDS is being considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE and CPA special timing and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-month window measurement differs for RCEs and CPAs: an IDS filed after the filing of an RCE will be considered if filed before the mailing date of a first Office action on the merits; CPAs likewise must have IDSs filed before the first Office action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCEs are treated as amended applications with short turnover time; applicants are encouraged to file any IDS with an RCE or CPA as early as possible, preferably at time of filing. If IDS cannot be filed before first action, applicants may request a three-month suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(b)/(c) and should notify the examiner if IDS is mailed shortly before suspension expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of submissions from other applications and improper reuse of forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are strongly discouraged from submitting copies of PTO/SB/08 or PTO-892 forms from other applications because completed forms may contain examiner initials and other application numbers that can confuse the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If spaces on an imported form already have initials, no space remains for the current examiner to initial; prior initials may be erroneously construed as applied for the current application.
